page.title: Best Window Security Camera (2026): Eufy E10 vs Botslab W101 vs Wyze
page.desc: Which camera actually works through glass at night: Eufy Window Camera E10, Botslab W101 and Wyze Window Cam compared on glare, night vision, free alerts and mounting, with prices checked 2026-11-06.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best window security camera for most people is the Eufy Window Camera E10: 2.5K video, free on-device person, vehicle and pet alerts, and a 25-degree downward tilt, for $79.99 at eufy.com on 2026-11-06. The best window camera that also watches the room is the Botslab W101 Window Camera ({buy:botslab-w101-window-camera}): two 2.5K lenses, one facing out and one facing into the room, with continuous recording to a microSD card up to 512 GB. The glare problem has one answer: all three cameras below skip infrared LEDs on the outward lens, so nothing bounces off the glass at night, but each needs some outdoor light such as a porch light or a streetlight.

The cheapest is the Wyze Window Cam at $34.98 (wyze.com, 2026-11-06): 1080p, 24/7 recording to a card with no plan, but person alerts need a paid Cam Plus plan, it is 2.4 GHz only, and the mounting sticker is single-use. If you already own a Wyze Cam OG, v3 or v4, the $3.99 Wyze Window Mount with night-vision IR switched off does the same job for less.

Battery cameras such as Blink Outdoor and Ring Stick Up Cam Battery are the wrong tool here: their passive-infrared motion sensors cannot see heat through glass, so they miss most motion outside. Every pick on this page is a plug-in camera that detects motion in the video itself.

page.after:
What owners complain about

  • Infrared glare. The most common complaint by far. A normal camera's IR LEDs bounce off the pane and white out the whole frame at night. The fix is a camera with no IR on the outward lens, or turning IR and the status light off in the app and pressing the lens to the glass.
  • Too dark without IR. Color night vision only works with some outdoor light. Owners of the Wyze Window Cam and Botslab W101 both report black footage in unlit yards; leave a porch light on.
  • Battery cameras miss motion. Blink and Ring battery cameras use passive-infrared sensors that cannot sense heat through glass. Blink's own support page says its cameras were not designed to detect motion through glass.
  • Screens, dirty glass and indoor lights. A window screen shows up as mesh and ruins focus; lamps and TVs behind the camera reflect in the pane. Pick a screenless window and keep the room darker than the outside.
  • Fixed aim. The Wyze and Botslab cameras sit flat against the glass, so a second-floor window shows mostly the far side of the driveway. The Eufy E10 tilts 25° down, which is why it leads for upstairs windows.
  • Stickers. Wyze's mounting stickers are single-use and hard to remove; Botslab's magnetic base lifts off its film pad for cleaning.

Which one by need

  • Driveway or porch from a ground-floor window, with free smart alerts: Eufy Window Camera E10. On-device person, vehicle and pet alerts without a plan, 2.5K with HDR, and the tilt dial.
  • One camera for the yard and the room behind it: Botslab W101 ({buy:botslab-w101-window-camera}). Its second lens gives a live infrared view of the room while the outward lens records 2.5K color footage to a card up to 512 GB. Remember the inward lens does not record.
  • Cheapest that just works: Wyze Window Cam at $34.98. 1080p and 2.4 GHz only, and smart alerts cost extra, but the glare-free housing and 24/7 card recording are there.
  • Already own a Wyze Cam: add the $3.99 Window Mount, set Night Vision to Off and disable the status light.

Not recommended

  • Blink Outdoor, Blink Mini, Ring Stick Up Cam Battery behind glass: PIR motion sensing fails through a window, and their IR lights glare.
  • Any IR-only indoor camera whose night vision cannot be switched off in the app; it will show you its own reflection all night.
  • The Botslab W101 as an indoor recorder. Its inward lens is live view only, so buy a normal indoor camera if you need indoor clips or indoor motion alerts.
